data.name: Karthika
data.gender_notes: Karthika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘kartika’, meaning ‘the night’. This name holds deep significance in Hindu mythology, as it is associated with the goddess Kartikeya, also known as Murugan or Skanda, who is the god of war and the son of Lord Shiva. The name Karthika carries the meaning “The night” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Karthika usually hope their child will grow to embody the night and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes new beginnings, courage, and protection.
data.etymology: Karthika belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “The night.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Karthika total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Karthika" brings to mind the fascinating Hindu mythology surrounding Kartikeya or Murugan, a revered deity known as the god of wars, knowledge, and human development. Karthika is often considered an auspicious name associated with the victory of good over evil, knowledge, and spiritual growth. In Hindu society, there are several cultural practices associated with this name. For instance, the Hindu month of Kartik (October-November), during which the festival of Diwali is celebrated, is believed to bring prosperity, success, and happiness to households. People born in this month are often named Karthika, and their birth is seen as a time of new beginnings and blessings. Furthermore, in some regions, a special traditional dance called "Karikalanattam" is performed in honor of Kartikeya during the Hindu temple festival of "Skanda Shashti".
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Karthika" holds immense power and meaning, as it is thought to be a divine name with deep spiritual connections. In Hinduism, Kartikeya is known as the God of auspiciousness, knowledge, and strength, who aids in spiritual development. The name Karthika represents purity, knowledge, and devotion. The air or vibrations around the name help in awakening the spiritual consciousness within a person. It is believed that chanting the name "Karthika" or meditating on the Kartikeya deity brings peace, contentment, and spiritual growth. Overall, the name Karthika carries both a cultural depth rooted in Hindu mythology and profound spiritual significance that inspires a deep sense of wisdom, knowledge, and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Karthika signifies the radiance of the Moon God (Chandra) during the auspicious occasion of the Karthik Maas (month). It is a symbol of inner illumination and spiritual growth, guiding one through the darkness towards enlightenment.

vedic_reference.note: Kartikeya, also known as Skanda, is a Hindu god and the god of war. Karthika is derived from Kartikeya.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Karthika is a Hindu name for the star Krittika in the constellation Ursa Major. The name Karthika carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

trends: Popular in India and among Indian communities worldwide
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Karthika remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.
